subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should OpenClaw pursue incremental session-memory indexing now, and if so should it be a fresh current-main implementation or a rescue of the open candidate PR?
rationale: The fix shape affects session-state correctness, memory_index schema behavior, source-wide batching, overlap semantics, and whether the existing proof-blocked branch is still worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade and real-behavior proof.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase and rework the open branch before reviewing it as the implementation path.

options.title: Defer incremental indexing
options.body: Accept the current cache and delta controls for now and close only after maintainers explicitly decide the complexity is not worth taking on.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade and real-behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged source-wide batching work is the strongest recent ownership signal for the current indexing path that an incremental fix must preserve.
